jobs.description:
Position Summary:
The Office of District Planning (ODP) is responsible for the development and implementation of district and borough based plans that address local needs and priorities with the goal of increasing access for all families to high quality educational options. These plans, developed in close partnership with superintendents, Community Education Councils (CECs), and local stakeholders, may include the opening of new schools, reconfigurations or re-sitings of existing schools, zoning changes, or openings of specialized programs (e.g. District 75, Autism NEST, Horizon and AIMS programs, etc.), among other levers.

The Senior Analyst of Data Strategy is responsible for developing and implementing policies and plans to optimize the use of space in New York City Public Schools (NYCPS), providing the infrastructure to ensure that students have access to high quality options. This work will include overseeing structural changes to schools to maximize the use of school facilities; crafting proposals to reduce overutilization; and designing various strategies to improve the use of school space and implement the Chancellor’s priorities.

Reports to:
Senior Director, Citywide Planning

Direct Reports:
District Planner

Key Relationships:
Works closely with other members of the Borough Planning Team and Analytics Team in District Planning as well as cross functional groups, including the Office of New School Development & Design (ONS), the Office of Student Enrollment (OSE), the Office of Space Management (OSM), the School Construction Authority (SCA), Office of Legal Services (OLS), and the Office of the First Deputy Chancellor (OFDC). Also develops relationships with key external stakeholders across the borough, including Community Superintendents, CECs, Community Boards, elected officials, principals, School Leadership Teams (SLTs) and Parent Associations to gather input in the decision making process.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning

Leads the development and implementation of district, borough and citywide policies and plans for structural changes intended to positively impact school performance, families’ access, and choice, learning conditions, and promote school integration and diversity.
Leads the maintenance for the strategic planning, design, development, and enhancement of all management information systems utilized by ODP.
Manages the development and review of Educational Impact Statements for all significant changes to school utilization, including the analysis of how proposed structural changes will impact school and neighborhood communities.
Supports the development and implementation of rezoning plans and other changes to school structure specifically designed to integrate and diversify NYCPS.
Oversees community engagement efforts around planning initiatives.
Supports data analysis related to mayoral and chancellor led initiatives, such as increasing enrollment across City schools, and prepares briefings and data analyses for Superintendents around these focus areas.
Analyzes impact of new legislation such as the New York State class size law and models scenarios for NYCPS to reach compliance.
Prioritizes and defines school planning and implementation work in a meaningful and actionable manner.
Allocates space and resources to existing high potential district and charter schools to sustain growth and quality.
Facilitates process for changing school zoning lines to increase choice and address overcrowding.

Cross functional Collaboration

Supports the Senior Director and Chief Executive Officer with all planning related efforts, specifically managing key internal and external relationships with NYCPS partner offices and other city agencies to field requests and communicate time sensitive information.
Assists with managing ongoing assessment of where additional capacity is needed, including working with SCA to identify and assess viability of lease sites.
Manages cross functional planning efforts around District 75 and other specialized programming to ensure we can meet demand across the city. Consults with other offices on District 75 travel analysis and the time and cost of transportation.
Serves as point for press team in generating planning related data as well as for Community Education Councils requesting school and district-level data.
Serves as a resource for local and state government agencies with an interest in educational opportunities.
Collaborates with other relevant city agencies (e.g., City Planning) to share information and best practices, to streamline data and resources.
Collaborates with OSE and the Division of Early Childhood Education to oversee all needs analysis for Pre-Kindergarten, 3-K, and other specialized programs citywide, including working through district channels to identify schools where programs can be established.
Manages collaboration with the OFDC to prepare data briefings for Superintendents to facilitate structural changes and interventions to schools.

Qualification Requirements

Minimum

A master’s degree from an accredited college in education, guidance, educational administration and supervision, or a related field and at least two (2) years of full-time satisfactory professional experience in educational program administration, career or occupational program administration, or as a state certified or licensed teacher, one (1) year of which must have been in a supervisory/consultative capacity; or
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and three (3) years of full-time satisfactory professional experience as described in “1” above; or
A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State's department of education or a recognized accrediting organization plus seven (7) years of full-time, satisfactory professional experience as described in “1” above; or
A combination of education and/or experience which is equivalent to the requirements in "1," "2," and “3” above. However, all candidates must have at least an approved four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent as well as the two (2) years of full-time satisfactory professional experience as described in “1” above.

Preferred

Ability to conduct data analysis around educational issues.
Creative problem solving skills with the ability to perform independently.
Experience with Microsoft SQL and knowledge of SQL tools and management techniques.
Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills in dealing with administrative/school based personnel.
Ability to work under pressure and effectively prioritize in a demanding environment.
Demonstrated interest and/or experience in education and public policy.
3+ years of experience in data management and analytics.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 applications.

jobs.title: Service Desk Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Americas Enterprise Technology is shifting from a support model that reacts to problems to one that anticipates and prevents them — and the EUS Technician is where that shift meets the employee in person. This role provides front-line deskside and walk-up support across our Chicago and New York locations, working hands-on with the hardware, software, and access issues that stand between an employee and a productive day — including the high-visibility, time-sensitive support our executives and VIP users expect.

The EUS Technician serves as the L2 escalation tier for the Birlasoft-operated L1 service desk, taking ownership of tickets that L1 cannot resolve — deeper hardware and software troubleshooting, device staging, and onboarding/offboarding — and coordinating with the Asset Management team on device deployment. This is a hands-on, in-office-first role for someone who takes ownership of the problem in front of them and is equally comfortable resolving an L2 escalation, staffing the Tech Bar, or flagging a device issue before the employee even notices it.

The right person for this role brings technical competence, patience with end users at every skill level, and a proactive mindset — someone who sees monitoring data and walk-up patterns as signals to act on, not just tickets to close.

What You Will Do

Deskside Support & Troubleshooting

Serve as the L2 escalation point for tickets routed from the Birlasoft L1 service desk, providing deeper diagnosis and hands-on resolution.
Provide hands-on troubleshooting and break/fix support for laptops, peripherals, and mobile devices.
Recognize and prioritize VIP and executive tickets appropriately, delivering prompt, high-touch resolution without being asked — understanding who needs to be served first and acting accordingly.
Own the L2 queue's SLA performance, ensuring escalated tickets move quickly from L1 handoff to resolution.
Escalate to the Global End User Computing Team (EUC), engineering, or vendor partners only when an issue is genuinely beyond L2 scope, ensuring a warm, confirmed handoff and follow-through.
Document resolution steps clearly in ServiceNow for every ticket worked, including root cause where L1 lacked one.

Onboarding, Offboarding & Asset Coordination

Prepare, image, and configure devices for new hires ahead of start date.
Execute offboarding device retrieval and wipe/reissue processes in coordination with Asset Management.
Maintain accurate device assignment records and flag discrepancies to the Asset Management team.

Tech Bar & Walk-Up Support

Staff walk-up Tech Bar hours, providing same-day resolution for common hardware and software issues.
Deliver a consistently professional, patient support experience for employees at every technical skill level.

Event & Pitch Support

Support onsite and offsite events and client pitches, partnering with the AV team and the Facilities Workplace Experience team on setup, troubleshooting, and live technical support.
Support executive setups and conference room technology and A/V needs as they arise.
Serve as the on-the-ground technical point of contact during high-visibility events, ensuring issues are resolved quickly and discreetly.

Proactive Device Health

Monitor device health signals (e.g., via Nexthink) to identify and resolve issues before they generate a ticket.
Escalate recurring device or software patterns to the EUS Manager for broader remediation.

Documentation & Knowledge Base

Maintain and contribute to knowledge base articles and SOPs for common issues and fixes.
Keep ticket documentation current enough that any teammate could pick up a ticket mid-stream.

Who You Are

You take ownership of the problem in front of you rather than routing it along, and you treat every employee interaction — whether a VP or a new hire — with the same patience and professionalism. You're comfortable working independently, prioritizing a shifting queue — including knowing instinctively when a ticket needs white-glove handling for an executive — and using data and monitoring tools to get ahead of issues rather than just reacting to them.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
3–5 years of experience in IT deskside support, service desk, or end user computing.

Required Qualifications

Hands-on experience with Windows and macOS device support, imaging, and troubleshooting.
Demonstrated experience operating as an L2 support tier — diagnosing issues L1 could not resolve and knowing when to escalate further.
Sound judgment in triaging support requests, including the ability to identify and prioritize VIP/executive tickets and deliver a consistently high-quality service experience for senior stakeholders.
Working knowledge of ServiceNow or a comparable ITSM ticketing platform.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and endpoint management tools including Intune and Entra ID.
Strong verbal communication skills — comfortable supporting employees at every level, including executives.
Ability to lift and move IT equipment and to be on-site full-time across supported locations.

What Will Set You Apart

Experience with DEX platforms such as Nexthink for proactive device health monitoring.
CompTIA A+, Network+, or equivalent certification.
Experience supporting a distributed, multi-site organization.
Familiarity with AV/conference room technology and executive support.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days, you know the tools, the ticket queue, the key stakeholders, and how work flows between L1, yourself, and Asset Management.

At 60 days, you're resolving deskside tickets independently, your documentation is clean, and the team trusts your follow-through on escalations.

At 90 days, you're a full contributor across Tech Bar, onboarding support, and proactive device health — not just keeping pace with the queue, but starting to get ahead of it.

At six months, you're a reliable presence at your site, known for turning a frustrating device issue into a fast, professional fix, and for catching problems before they reach the employee.

jobs.title: Fixed Income Division - Analyst or Associate, Municipal Markets (New York)
jobs.description:
Join a quantitative team supporting a large municipal bond market-making desk. We work alongside traders across electronic and voice trading, bond origination, specialized lending, and bespoke derivative products.

Our team uses mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and software to solve practical trading problems. We analyze trading strategies, build electronic trading algorithms, model the financial risks associated with the desk’s inventory, and conduct detailed analysis of trading profits and losses.

Municipal markets offer particularly interesting quantitative challenges. Many securities trade infrequently, bonds differ across numerous structural features, and available market data can be incomplete. We develop mathematical models that connect observable market variables to bond prices, helping the trading desk estimate value, identify relative-value opportunities, manage risk, and make better trading decisions.

The Role

As a Quantitative Strategist, you will work directly with traders, quantitative researchers, and engineers. You will use data and statistical analysis to identify potential trading strategies, assist with complex trades and hedging decisions, and improve the models and systems used to price securities and monitor risk.

You will also help organize and maintain the team’s quantitative research environment, including its modeling software, research archive, Python packages, Linux environment, containers and testing. The role includes both immediate desk-facing analysis and longer-term research into trading strategies and market behavior.

Responsibilities

Research and test quantitative trading strategies.
Help traders evaluate complex transactions, hedge selection, position sizing, and execution timing.
Develop pricing and risk models for municipal bonds, bond derivatives, and related products.
Analyze inventory risk, trading activity, and profit-and-loss performance.
Apply statistics and machine learning to trading, pricing, and risk-management problems.
Help move machine-learning and AI models into production.
Organize and maintain quantitative models, research code, and development environments.
Communicate analytical findings clearly to traders and other stakeholders.

Qualifications

new_jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Marketing at Brex

The Marketing team tells the Brex story, turning product innovation into customer obsession. We develop messaging, shape the brand, and bring our platform to life through thoughtful, compelling content. Our team spans Revenue Marketing, Product Marketing, and Brand Marketing, and works cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Business Development, and Design to drive growth and build trust.

What you'll do

You will lead the systems, data, and operations that turn demand into qualified sales conversations and help Marketing make better investment decisions. Your operating mandate runs from lead capture through qualified meetings; your measurement mandate extends through pipeline and closed revenue.

Partnering with the Senior Director of Growth Marketing, you will build the team and set the technical roadmap for a more reliable, scalable funnel across enterprise sales and self-serve motions, including Brex and Capital One integrations.

In your first year, you will establish baselines and targets with Growth Marketing, Revenue Operations, and SDR leadership to improve meaningful follow-up, routing accuracy, qualified meetings, and meeting-to-opportunity conversion, while building trusted funnel data and faster campaign delivery.

Where you'll work

This role will be based in one of our hubs: San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Salt Lake City, or Vancouver. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end marketing funnel from demand capture through sales handoff, including qualification, enrichment, scoring, routing, automation, and measurement.
Partner with SDR, RevOps, Product, Engineering, and Data Science to improve funnel throughput, speed-to-lead, conversion, and reliability.
Design scalable workflows across sales-led and self-serve motions, including emerging Capital One lead sources.
Own the marketing technology ecosystem and integrations across Marketo, Salesforce, LeanData, web/CMS, analytics, advertising, and other GTM platforms.
Set the architecture and operating standards that ensure systems are scalable, reliable, and connected.
Lead major platform improvements and evaluate new capabilities, including CDP and AI-enabled workflows.
Own the quality and governance of marketing and prospect data, including identity, enrichment, segmentation, taxonomy, and attribution.
Establish trusted funnel and performance measurement in partnership with RevOps, Finance, Data, and Engineering.
Translate data into recommendations that improve marketing efficiency, sales handoffs, and investment decisions.
Lead and develop the Marketing Operations team while establishing clear priorities, operating rhythms, service levels, and accountability.
Build scalable processes for intake, prioritization, capacity planning, documentation, and execution.
Serve as a highly autonomous thought partner to Growth Marketing leadership and drive alignment across Marketing, Sales, RevOps, Product, Engineering, and Finance.

Requirements

8+ years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or growth operations, including 3+ years leading and developing a team.
Measurable improvements to lead-to-meeting conversion, with experience supporting both enterprise sales and self-serve or product-led motions.
Deep hands-on architecture experience in Marketo or an equivalent marketing automation platform, plus strong Salesforce fluency and shared platform ownership with Revenue Operations.
Experience designing scalable lifecycle, scoring, routing, campaign taxonomy, and data governance practices.
Strong measurement judgment, including understanding attribution limitations, plus SQL and BI fluency to investigate performance independently.
A track record of using pipeline or forecast models to inform decisions and aligning cross-functional partners on execution.
Experience managing martech vendors and increasing team capacity through automation and reusable processes.
Experience running marketing systems as production infrastructure, including monitoring, incident response, and change control on revenue-facing workflows.
Experience running intake and prioritization for a team serving many internal stakeholders, with capacity planning that holds up under pressure.

Bonus points

Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment.
Technical partnership with Product and Engineering on signup flows or identity resolution.
Experience with holdouts, incrementality testing, or media mix modeling.
Experience with marketing financial planning and reporting.
AI or agent-assisted workflows with measurable results.
Hands-on experience with LeanData, Qualified, Hex, a customer data platform, or integration and workflow tools such as Retool.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $185,320 - $231,650. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate's location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.
